incident_2024_09_12_outage:
ROOT CAUSE: A Web-channel-specific service disruption on 2024-09-12. Web revenue fell 77.2% versus its trailing 7-day baseline while Mobile App was essentially flat (+0.2%) and Marketplace was actually up (+7.1%), which rules out a demand-side cause (a real demand drop would hit all channels roughly proportionally) and points squarely at something broken in the Web checkout/payment path specifically. Total daily revenue fell 33.7%, consistent with Web's ~46% baseline revenue share being almost entirely wiped out for the day.

CONFIDENCE: High — the effect is large (-77%), isolated to exactly one channel, and recovered fully the next day, the classic signature of an outage rather than a demand or pricing issue.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Pull Web-channel error logs and payment-gateway status for 2024-09-12 to confirm and root-cause the outage; if confirmed, add a same-day automated alert on any single-channel revenue drop >50% vs. trailing baseline so this class of incident is caught within hours, not the next morning.
incident_2024_11_29_promo_spike:
ROOT CAUSE: A West-region-specific promotional event during the Nov 29-Dec 1 Black Friday/Cyber Monday window. All regions saw a holiday lift (Midwest +33.6%, Northeast +27.3%, South +36.6% vs. baseline), consistent with company-wide seasonal demand — but West is a clear outlier at +240.3%, roughly 7x the lift every other region saw. That gap is too large to be explained by general seasonality alone and points to a region-specific driver (e.g. a West-only promo code, a regional marketing push, or a local event).

CONFIDENCE: High — the pattern (universal moderate lift + one region massively above the rest) cleanly separates a general seasonal effect from a region-specific cause.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Confirm with the marketing/promotions team whether a West-region-specific offer ran during this window; if so, this is a positive result worth understanding for replication in other regions, not an issue to fix. Tag it in the incident log as 'informational / positive' rather than a problem.
incident_2025_02_south_drift:
ROOT CAUSE: A sustained, South-region-specific revenue decline beginning early February 2025. Over the Feb 1-21 window, South revenue is down 16.8% versus its Jan 1-21 baseline while every other region is flat to slightly up (Midwest +5.0%, Northeast +4.2%, West +6.6%) — an isolated regional decline, not a company-wide softening. Notably, TOTAL daily revenue across all regions moved only -1.2% over the same window, meaning this incident was essentially invisible at the aggregate level and was only caught because the regional-drift detector checks each region's trend independently rather than relying on the total.

CONFIDENCE: Medium-High — the regional isolation is clear and the decline is sustained (not a single bad day), but the diagnostic playbook run here doesn't have visibility into external factors (competitor activity, local economic conditions, a regional operational issue) that would confirm the specific cause, only that it's a real, region-specific, sustained effect.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Escalate to the South-region commercial team to check for local competitive activity, regional stock-outs, or a regional pricing/support issue; separately, this incident is a strong argument for monitoring regional trend lines as a standing dashboard view, not only the company total, since a 17% regional decline was otherwise invisible for three full weeks.
incident_2024_12_22_holiday_ramp_false_p:
ROOT CAUSE: This flag does not appear to reflect a real, isolated incident. Region breakdown shows every region moving in the same direction and within a similar range of the others (no single region diverging sharply), and the same is true across channels — the signature of a broad, company-wide pattern rather than something localized. This is consistent with the anomaly detector's 7-day seasonal model lagging the fast, large step-up in demand at the start of the holiday period (a level shift within a couple of weeks is hard for a rolling weekly-seasonality model to absorb immediately), producing residual spikes as the model's trend estimate catches up — not a new operational event.

CONFIDENCE: Medium — the uniform-movement evidence is a reliable signal that this isn't an isolated cause, but confirming it's specifically a seasonality-modeling artifact (versus, say, a genuine platform-wide but still real effect) would need a longer look-back check against last year's same-week pattern, which isn't available in this diagnostic pass.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: No incident response needed. Log as a known false-positive class ('holiday-ramp seasonality lag') and consider adding a holiday calendar feature to the detector so late-November through December isn't flagged on this pattern every year.
